About London Advanced

London, looked at twice.

London Advanced is an independent guide, community and set of practical tools for people who want to move beyond the standard list and understand more of the city around them.

Based in LondonSince 2018
Explored personally900+ places
The Other London124 pages
Practical access5 free tools
01Paolo

I built the guide I wanted to use.

I’m Paolo Pastorino, the founder and editor of London Advanced. I moved to London in 2018 and have spent nearly eight years exploring it on foot, by bicycle, bus and Tube.

That exploration became a personal map of more than 900 places within the M25: overlooked buildings, small museums, gardens, oddities, views, markets, religious spaces and neighbourhoods that reward curiosity. The collection began with places I had visited, researched and photographed rather than locations gathered simply to make a longer list.

I am interested in the London that hides in plain sight: not necessarily secret, but easy to miss when the same landmarks and recommendations are repeated everywhere.

02Purpose

Beyond the obvious does not mean obscure for its own sake.

London Advanced is for curious residents, repeat visitors and first-time visitors willing to look beyond the default itinerary. The aim is not to reject famous London, but to make the rest of the city easier to discover and more practical to explore.

A place belongs here when it offers a worthwhile story, atmosphere, detail or experience—and when the information helps somebody make a better decision about going. That is why the project combines editorial recommendations with practical tools for crowds, fares, routes, live conditions and discovery by mood.

The editorial test

Would I tell a curious friend to spend part of their London day here—and can I explain why?

03The project

One idea, expressed in different ways.

The Other London is the 124-page field guide at the centre of the project. It brings together handpicked places, original photography, practical access information, map links and nearby suggestions across eight broad sections.

The website’s five free tools answer more immediate questions: use the London Dashboard for live conditions, compare expected crowd pressure, calculate London travel fares, find worthwhile detours along a route, or choose places by mood.

The Facebook group and Instagram account extend the same work into a community: a place to share discoveries, photographs, questions and updates rather than treating the guide as a finished list.

04Selection

Curated, checked and allowed to remain subjective.

Places are selected for a combination of character, story, visual or historical interest, local distinctiveness and practical value. Personal visits and original photography underpin the core collection; official sources are used to check details that may change.

Event recommendations follow a separate process. They must fit the London Advanced point of view, meet the published value threshold and be verified against an organiser, venue or other authoritative source before publication. The selected weekend edit is deliberately small rather than pretending to be a complete listings service.

The judgement is editorial. Not everybody will find the same place quiet, beautiful, strange or worth a detour, and the site does not pretend otherwise. The Methodology page explains the evidence, scoring and limitations in more detail.

05Independence

The recommendations are not for sale.

London Advanced is independently created and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the places included in the guide or tools. Venues do not pay to enter the collection or to receive a favourable description.

The project does have commercial elements. The Other London is a paid guide, and some clearly identified ticket links may be affiliate links. If an eligible purchase produces a commission, it does not increase the price paid by the reader. Commercial relationships do not determine which places or editorial events are selected.

Simple rule

If money may be earned from a link, the relationship should be visible before somebody uses it.
